fields.why:
New TSF3 will be cut over in January shut, and downtime in the event of a blockage is significantly greater than current setup. To mitigate this downtime in the event of loss of tailings flow, an auto failover to standby line is needed. This Failover will prioritise the flushing of the discharge pipeline to the TSF over the conditioning on the local pump skid.

The proposed plan is for these sequences to be automatically initiated on edge case failures (i.e. total pump failure) and will not be able to manually started. However, the sequence will be tested via manual start while running on water during the October shut.
fields.design:
There are 3 parts to this change request.
1) Modification of tails system reduce possibility of line blockage via
 a) Pump interlock modifications
 b) Valve trip condition modifications
2) New failover sequence to trigger as required (TBD)

1A - PUMP INTERLOCK MODIFCATIONS
Create two new sequences which when activated will automatically flush and changeover from Tails Line A to Tails Line B (236-SEQ-677B) and from Tails Line B to Tails Line A (236-SEQ-678B).
As Part of New sequences, Pump and Valve interlocks will be modified as per below (Modifications in BOLD):

Pump 1
A) Start Permissives
 i) (Gland Flow Switch Healthy
 ii) AND Booster Pumps Running
 iii) OR Failover Sequence Running)
 iv) Suction Valve OR Flushing Valve Opened
 v) Suction Drain Valve Closed
B) Process Interlocks
 i) Gland Flow Switch Trip Timeout not complete – Remove Interlock and Upgrade Trip alarm to Critical Severity
 ii) Tails Tank Level not Low
 iii) Suction Valve OR Flushing Valve Open Requested
 iv) Suction Drain Valve Close Requested
 v) Pump 2 Running (with startup masking)
 vi) RIO Comms Fault – Remove
 vii) Module Comms Fault – Remove
C) Critical Interlocks
 i) No Changes

Pump 2
A) Start Permissives
 i) (Gland Flow Switch Healthy
 ii) AND Booster Pumps Running)
 iii) OR Failover Sequence Running
 iv) Opposite Line Discharge Valve Closing- Closed
 v) Discharge Valve Opened
B) Process Interlocks
 i) Pump 1 Running
 ii) Gland Flow Switch Trip Timeout not complete – Remove and Upgrade Trip alarm to Critical Severity
 iii) Tails Pressure not High High – Remove
 iv) Gland Water Booster Pumps Running – Remove
 v) Discharge Valve Open Requested
 vi) Opposite Line discharge valve Close requested
 vii) Tails Discharge Pressure Transmitter not out of range – Remove
 viii) RIO Comms Fault – Remove
 ix) Module Comms Fault (x2) – Remove
C) Critical Interlocks
 i) No Changes

1B - VALVE TRIP CONDITION MODIFICATIONS
Line A and Line B flushing valves will have following trip open condition added to existing:
 Line in service AND Tails Tank Level Low Alarm Active
Line A and Line B suction valves will have following trip closed condition added to existing:
 Line in service AND Tails Tank Level Low Alarm Active

2 - FAILOVER SEQUENCE
*Given the reason for this change unless otherwise stated, sequence transitions on valve positions will look at a confirmation of move away from current position, rather than confirmed required position state (i.e. Close Discharge Valve is assumed successful when open position proxy is lost).
*Local line flushing will not take place during sequence shutdown of failed line due to line pressurization priority.

Upon failure trigger (i.e. when pumps 1A & 1B or 2A & 2B have stopped) sequence will take following actions:
1) Action: Simultaneously operate failed line valves
 a) Close Suction Valve
 b) Open Suction Drain Valve
 c) Close Gland Water Valves on both failed line pumps
 d) Close Discharge Valve
 Transition: Actions from a) initiated AND Positive confirmation of discharge valve closed OR 45s (TBC) after loss of discharge valve open proxy
2) Action: Start Gland Water Booster Pump
 Transition: Gland water booster pump start requested
3) Action: Simultaneously operate standby line valves
 a) Close suction drain valve
 b) Open flushing valve
 d) Open Gland Water Valves on both pumps
 Transition: Suction and Flushing Valve positions have changed state and open is requested for gland water valves
4) Action: Set Pump 1 Speed to Startup Speed Setpoint (TBC)
 Transition: SP Confirmed
5) Action: Start Pump 1
 Transition: Pump 1 running
6) Action: Open Discharge Valve
 Transition: Discharge Valve opened confirmed
7) Action: Set Pump 1 Power Controller to Auto at Startup Power Setpoint (TBC)
 Transition: SP Confirmed
8) Action: Set Pump 2 Flow Controller to Auto Startup Speed Setpoint (TBC)
 Transition: SP Confirmed
9) Action: Start Pump 2
 Transition: Pump 2 running
10) Action: Start Flushing Timer (TBC)
 Transition: Timer Completed
11) Action: Open Suction Valve
 Transition: Suction Valve Opened feedback
12) Action: Close Flush Valve
 Transition: Flush Valve Closed feedback
